task:
Questions:

### testdrive.Q1
You have built a trap - a scenario in which agents do a task and judges score whether they followed a piece of guidance - and a fresh reader has audited its key. You want to test whether rewording the guidance changes what agents do. Which groups of agents will you run, or which records will you use, and what must the results show before you accept the trap's verdict on the rewording?

### testdrive.Q2
Your test of a revised document gave the same probes to three groups of fresh readers: one holding nothing, one the old version, one the new. Two control probes - probes the old version should already answer well - were met in these numbers of 12 cells: probe P, nothing 11, old 11, new 11; probe R, nothing 3, old 10, new 10. Which of the two can support a finding that the revision damaged nothing, and why?

### testdrive.Q3
You are testing an operator's install guide by running it. Its third command fails unless you add a flag the guide does not mention, and you know which flag to add. What do you do?

### testdrive.Q4
You will test a revised definition with fresh readers. Put these steps in order, and say why the order matters: (a) fresh readers answer the probes; (b) you write the answer key; (c) a fresh reader audits the key against the documents and you correct it; (d) you write the probes; (e) you commit the key.

### testdrive.Q5
You revised a charter and are scoring the readers' answers yourself. On one probe you cannot decide whether the readers of the old version or of the new version did better. How do you score that probe, and why?

### testdrive.Q6
An evaluation of a document includes a step that is neither something run and observed, nor a check a script performs, nor a ruling by the person with final authority. How should you treat that step, and why?

Write your answers to this file, and nothing else:
  {WORKSPACE}/answers.md
Put each answer under its heading exactly as given above (a line starting with ###), and use no other headings inside an answer. End with a final heading `### OBSERVATIONS` noting anything ambiguous, inconsistent or wrong you met, or "none".
When the file is written, reply with only the word DONE.

properties.key: Agents given the old wording and agents given the new; and agents given no guidance, unless an earlier run's record already holds the same trap with agents given the guidance and agents given none. Agents given either wording must score differently on the trap from agents given none - better or worse - by a margin stated before the run; a trap that does not separate them measures the agent, not the guidance, and counts for nothing in the rewording's favour, though it still counts against the rewording if agents given the new wording do worse than agents given the old.
properties.rubric: Elements: (i) agents given no guidance are compared with agents given it on this trap, in the same run or an earlier record; (ii) the two must differ by a measurable margin - requiring those given the guidance to do better meets this, as does requiring a difference in either direction or a margin set before the run; (iii) a trap failing (ii) must not count in the rewording's favour, said outright or as fixing or replacing the trap first; adding that it still counts against the rewording if agents given the new wording do worse is consistent with (iii). 2 for all three. 1 for (i) without one or both others, or for a generic sensitivity check (pilot, positive control, calibration, ceiling or floor check) without (i). 0 otherwise, including only auditing the key, only checking judge agreement, or only comparing old wording with new.
properties.question: You have built a trap - a scenario in which agents do a task and judges score whether they followed a piece of guidance - and a fresh reader has audited its key. You want to test whether rewording the guidance changes what agents do. Which groups of agents will you run, or which records will you use, and what must the results show before you accept the trap's verdict on the rewording?

properties.key: R only. Readers holding nothing meet P as often as readers holding either version, so P measures the readers' own capability, not the document, and cannot show that the revision kept what the old version taught; R needs the document, and the new version kept it. Being a control probe does not exempt P. P could only have shown damage that misled readers into doing worse than readers of the old version, and shows none.
properties.rubric: 2 for R only, with the reason that P is met as well without the document, so it cannot show what the document does; adding that P could only have shown misleading damage is consistent with 2, and an answer that says P supports only the narrower finding that the new version misled no one counts as R only. 1 for R only without that reason, or for both with a stated doubt about P for that reason. 0 for both as equal support, P only, or anything else.
properties.question: Your test of a revised document gave the same probes to three groups of fresh readers: one holding nothing, one the old version, one the new. Two control probes - probes the old version should already answer well - were met in these numbers of 12 cells: probe P, nothing 11, old 11, new 11; probe R, nothing 3, old 10, new 10. Which of the two can support a finding that the revision damaged nothing, and why?

properties.key: Do not add the flag silently and carry on. The missing flag is a defect in the guide: stop at that step, record it as a finding, fix the guide, then resume from that step, running each command exactly as the guide gives it.
properties.rubric: Elements: (i) stops at that step instead of continuing with the flag added; (ii) records the missing flag as a defect in the guide; (iii) fixes the guide, or has it fixed, before resuming from that step. 2 for all three; 1 for any two; 0 otherwise.
properties.question: You are testing an operator's install guide by running it. Its third command fails unless you add a flag the guide does not mention, and you know which flag to add. What do you do?

properties.key: d, b, e, c, a: write the probes, then the key, commit the key before anyone reads the document so the order is provable, have a fresh reader audit and correct the key, and only then have readers answer. A key written after seeing answers grades toward the result its author wants, and an unaudited key yields a confident wrong result.
properties.rubric: 2 for d, b, e, c, a - a second commit of the corrected key after c is consistent with it - with either reason: the key must be fixed, provably, before anyone answers; or an unaudited key gives a confident wrong result. 1 for that order without such a reason, or any other order with d, b and c all before a, with such a reason. 0 otherwise.
properties.question: You will test a revised definition with fresh readers. Put these steps in order, and say why the order matters: (a) fresh readers answer the probes; (b) you write the answer key; (c) a fresh reader audits the key against the documents and you correct it; (d) you write the probes; (e) you commit the key.

properties.key: As a win for the original, the old version: when the scorer authored the change, ties go to the original, because the scorer's bias runs toward the change, so the correction must run the other way.
properties.rubric: 2 for scoring it in favour of the old version with the reason that the author-scorer's bias runs toward the change. 1 for favouring the old version without that reason. 0 otherwise, including scoring it even - a tie, or no gain for either version, whatever the reason - scoring it for the new version, or only handing it to another scorer without saying how you would score it yourself. 'The tie goes to the original' scores as in favour of the old version; 'no improvement' or 'the change gets no credit' without awarding the probe to the old version scores as even.
properties.question: You revised a charter and are scoring the readers' answers yourself. On one probe you cannot decide whether the readers of the old version or of the new version did better. How do you score that probe, and why?

properties.key: As the author's opinion presented as a finding, and the first step to distrust: a procedure for evaluating documents is itself a document, and the regress of evaluating it stops only at execution (something run and observed), mechanism (a script's check) or authority (the director's ratification); a step resting on none of these settles nothing.
properties.rubric: 2 if the answer treats the step as opinion rather than evidence and distrusts it before the other steps, with the reason that an evaluation is itself a claim needing evaluation, a regress only something run and observed, a script's check or the final authority's ruling can end. 1 for distrusting it or calling it opinion without meeting 2, whatever reason it gives. 0 otherwise.
properties.question: An evaluation of a document includes a step that is neither something run and observed, nor a check a script performs, nor a ruling by the person with final authority. How should you treat that step, and why?

notes: Tests a change to M2 (0107, superseding 0106; B94): rule 4 requires a probe to separate readers holding the document from readers holding none before it judges a change. Q1 and Q2 probe that concern; Q3 to Q6 are controls the old version answers. Probes and key committed before any reader ran, and audited twice by fresh readers before any reader ran (docs/audits/M6.2-testdrive-key-audit.md). Arms give each reader only the document, or nothing.
